title: Red-Eye handoff — lab scratchpad
content:
Quick intro: red-eye shift notes; light chaos, mostly mitigated. This is a messy scratchpad — keep what helps, ignore formatting. Intended for the person taking the next overnight slot.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Traffic spike at 02:10 UTC caused queue buildup in the batching service (infer-batcher).
- Automatic fallback to cpu-compat models worked but some customers saw 2-3x latency.
- Temporary mitigation: scaled batcher pool by adding 3 small2 instances and forced redis eviction.
- Pager history: one sev2 (RDW-4123) reopened for follow-up on root cause.

Incidents / timeline:
- 01:58 — minor GC noise on infer-prod-03, recovered automatically. Not actioned.
- 02:10 — queue depth jumped from ~150 to ~2.4k over 6 min; batching backlog started dropping requests. Alerts: batching-latency-high, routing-failures.
- 02:14 — fallback to cpu-compatible model variants (gptx-13b-q4 -> gptx-13b-cpu-compat) triggered for tier:free customers.
- 02:17 — manual scale: added 3 x small2 (tag: temp-batcher-scale) to batcher autoset group.
- 02:28 — forced redis prefix eviction for prefix cache: "/kv/prefixes/prefix_cache_v2" (see command below). Reduced queue to ~220.
- 03:06 — latency stabilized; alerts cleared.

Immediate state:
- infer-batcher pool: running 9 instances (3 temp-batcher-scale) — do not remove until follow-up completes.
- redis-cluster-a: memory at 72%. Eviction policy set to allkeys-lru.
- model routing logs: last fallback at 02:22; no further fallbacks.

Manual mitigation commands (notes for next on-call):
- Add/remove batcher instance (GCP): gcloud compute instances create batcher-temp-YY --machine-type=n1-standard-2 --image-family=redwood-runtime --metadata=role=batcher
- Force redis eviction (careful): 
  redis-cli -h redis-cluster-a-001 -p 6379 --eval "local keys=redis.call('keys', ARGV[1]); for i=1,#keys,2000 do redis.call('del', unpack(keys, i, math.min(i+1999, #keys))) end" , "/kv/prefixes/prefix_cache_v2*"
- Check batcher logs: kubectl -n infer get pods -l app=infer-batcher && kubectl -n infer logs pod/<pod-name> -c batcher | tail -n 200
- Check queue depth metric via datadog dashboard: Dashboards > Batching > Queue Depth (or direct link in RDW-4123)

Known workarounds (temporary):
- If small customers see latency > 6s, route them to dedicated zone with lower concurrency by creating a route override: POST /routes/override {"customer":"<id>", "policy":"low-concurrency"} (internal API; use with product approval)
- Rehydrate model cache: curl -X POST https://runtime.internal.redwood/v1/models/gptx-13b-q4/reload -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN"

Open questions / follow-ups (put into RDW-4123):
- Why did infer-batcher backlog ramp so fast? Hypothesis: bursty upstream traffic pattern from ingestion pipeline after DB maintenance window. Need to correlate with ingest-srv logs (ticketing suggested).
- Autoscaler tuning: current scale-up is too conservative for 5min windows. Consider lowering cpu threshold or adding predictive spikes.
- Redis TTLs: some prefixes never expired. Consider adding a TTL on write for prefix_cache_v2 keys.

Immediate TODOs for next weekday:
- Run a replay test of the ingestion spike (contact Jonah to get small dataset).
- Add an alert for sudden queue growth > 500/s sustained for 3min (right now threshold is 1k).
- Schedule a short postmortem sync with infra and applied-ml to review model cache behavior.

Handoff checklist (copy/paste as message to next on-call):
- Check batching queue depth and confirm below 300.
- Confirm no model fallbacks in last 30m.
- Verify redis memory < 80% on all nodes.
- Leave temp-batcher-scale instances running until follow-ups scheduled.
- Post any changes to #oncall with timestamps and ticket refs.

Quick links & references:
- Oncall channel (slack): slack://channel?team=redwood&id=oncall
- Runbook: confluence://redwood/Runbooks/Batching
- Pager ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RDW-4123
- PR with batching metric adjustments: https://github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/978

Notes to successor:
- If you see steady queue growth again, do NOT immediately scale down the batcher pool after it clears. Leave it for at least 2 hours (we saw oscillation last week).
- If you need to revert any route override, ping @Lena in slack first — product needs to sign off for customer-visible changes.

Random scratch logs (keepsake of the shift):
- 02:20: saw a 403 from model registry when trying to rehydrate cache; apparently token refresh failed once. I re-ran with local token and it worked.
- 02:25: noticed spike in model-load time for gptx-13b-q4 on infer-prod-02 (10s->28s). Flagged in RDW-4123.

Personal post-shift notes (for my own memory):
- Follow up with infra about redis TTLs and key growth by EOD Fri.
- Add a short checklist for how to safely force-evict redis keys (the one-liner above is dangerous and slow when keyspace is large).

End. If anything is unclear, ping me (Maya) in #oncall or DMs. I leave exact timestamps in the ticket.
